title: Hark previews its browser use agent for completing tasks
excerpt: Hark claims that its browser use agent is faster and cheaper than competition.
content_html:
Hark, a startup that raised $700 million in Series A funding in May, today launched its agent Hark Handoff, which can use a browser efficiently to complete tasks.

The company claims that Handoff can easily navigate websites that have no official APIs, including Target, Walmart, OpenTable, and LinkedIn. It said that the Handoff agent looks at website structure and visual data to understand if it needs to click buttons or type information.

The premise is similar to tons of browser-based agents released before. Issue a command, and it will complete tasks for you, including ordering food or coffee, booking travel tickets, filing returns, shopping for essentials, reserving a table at a restaurant, or researching on your behalf by looking at various sources.

In a video demo, the company’s CEO, Brett Adcock, showed that the assistant can take a command to build a bouquet with flowers users specify, along with accommodating fuzzy terms like “some of the florist’s choice.” Notably, the video shows only part of the process, so we can’t really gauge its effectiveness.

The company said that for this release, it’s using a post-trained model, and plans to pre-train later this year. Hark said that, with this approach, it can refine its data pipeline, training infrastructure, and techniques more quickly. Hark also claims that, unlike large language models (LLMs) predicting the next token, its model can predict the next action — which could be a clock or a keyboard input at a specific place.

There are many companies working on computer-use agents, including Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic, with VC-funded startups working on browser-based task automation, such as Browser Use, Polar, Strawberry, and Aside.

Hark said that its Handoff agent is faster than the competition and also costs much less than other models like GPT 5.5 and Opus 4.8. The startup has opened a waitlist for its platform and plans to release it by the end of the summer.

content_html_zh:
Hark 是一家在 5 月份筹集了 7 亿美元 A 轮融资的初创公司，今天推出了其代理 Hark Handoff，它可以高效地使用浏览器来完成任务。

该公司声称，Handoff 可以轻松浏览没有官方 API 的网站，包括 Target、Walmart、OpenTable 和 LinkedIn。 据称，Handoff 代理会查看网站结构和视觉数据，以了解是否需要单击按钮或键入信息。

前提类似于之前发布的大量基于浏览器的代理。 发出命令，它就会为您完成任务，包括订购食物或咖啡、预订旅行机票、提交退货、购买必需品、在餐厅预订餐桌或通过查看各种来源来代表您进行研究。

在视频演示中，该公司的首席执行官布雷特·阿德科克 (Brett Adcock) 展示了助手可以接受命令，用用户指定的鲜花制作花束，并适应“花店的一些选择”等模糊术语。 值得注意的是，视频仅显示了部分过程，因此我们无法真正评估其有效性。

该公司表示，在这个版本中，它使用的是后训练模型，并计划在今年晚些时候进行预训练。 Hark 表示，通过这种方法，它可以更快地完善其数据管道、培训基础设施和技术。 Hark 还声称，与预测下一个标记的大型语言模型 (LLM) 不同，它的模型可以预测下一个动作——可能是特定位置的时钟或键盘输入。

有许多公司致力于计算机使用代理，包括 Google、OpenAI 和 Anthropic，还有风投资助的初创公司致力于基于浏览器的任务自动化，例如 Browser Use、Polar、Strawberry 和 Aside。

Hark 表示，其 Handoff 代理比竞争对手更快，而且成本也比 GPT 5.5 和 Opus 4.8 等其他模型低得多。 该初创公司已为其平台设立了候补名单，并计划在夏末之前发布。
